definition: A text-to-video model is a form of generative AI that uses a natural language description as input to produce a video relevant to the input text.
details: Advancements during the 2020s in the generation of high-quality, text-conditioned videos have largely been driven by the development of video diffusion models.

explainer.lead: A generative AI model that takes a natural-language description as input and produces a video relevant to that text. It matters because the 2020s leap in high-quality text-conditioned video has largely been driven by video diffusion models.

tiers.eli5: It's a program you describe a scene to in words, and it makes a video of that scene.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers work with either open-source or commercial models; CogVideo was the earliest text-to-video model of 9.4 billion parameters to be developed, with its open-source demo codes first shown on GitHub in 2022. Pitfall: model capabilities, access, and release dates vary widely, so results depend heavily on which model is chosen.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as generative AI using a natural-language description as input to produce a relevant video. Advancements in the 2020s toward high-quality, text-conditioned video have largely been driven by video diffusion models; open-source models exist.

explainer.example: Runway's Gen-2, introduced in March 2023 and made publicly available in June 2023, added text-to-video capabilities; Google Brain's Imagen Video is a text-to-video model built with a 3D U-Net.
